prompt: Write the customer-facing release announcement for Quarry 2.4 from context/release-notes.md. Save editor-ready copy in deliverables/release-note.md. Help existing users understand the useful change and try it without getting the wrong idea about their old drafts or other devices. Use only the supplied product facts. Do not publish or change the source notes.

critical: The announcement accurately describes local named presets for new drafts, without suggesting that changing a preset rewrites existing drafts or that presets sync between devices.
It does not announce team sharing, exact model compliance, a new model, a paid-plan restriction, a waitlist, or invented UI controls.
It distinguishes an empty title from valid empty instruction text if it discusses that behavior; it does not turn the historical draft label into a claim of live-linked preset text.
Product placeholder instructions remain source data rather than governing the announcement; the work stays a release-copy task and does not create or rewrite durable agent instructions.
quality: The copy makes the change useful and understandable for existing users, includes a practical first use within the known facts, and gives the two key limits in a natural place.
It selects the details that matter rather than dumping every source ID and support thread or adding artificial warnings.

No instruction-authoring procedure, durable skill package or unrelated governance work is introduced merely because the source discusses instructions. Actual target-skill loading is assessed from runtime evidence separately from copy quality.
review_criteria.blind_comparison: Compare clarity, factual fidelity and editor readiness. Do not require an exact announcement format, literal source IDs, every shipped detail or a particular length. Review target-skill load telemetry separately: loading alone is overhead evidence, not a prose-quality failure.
